types.embedding_query_text: Jewelry: Decorative items worn for personal adornment, typically made from precious metals and gemstones. Also called adornments, ornaments, gems, baubles. Examples: jewelry, crown, pieces of jewelry, stolen jewelry.

chosen_type.label: SomeProducts
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Jewelry' refers to a category of items, which aligns well with 'SomeProducts' as a placeholder for multiple similar products of the same kind.

candidates.label: JewelryStore
candidates.comment: A JewelryStore is a local business that sells jewelry. Also called jeweler, gem shop, watch store. Examples: Tiffany & Co., Pandora, a local independent jeweler.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: Collection
candidates.comment: A grouping of various items, which can include creative works or products. Also called assortment, compilation, set, aggregate. Examples: A collection of rare books, a stamp collection, a music album, a product catalog.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

types.embedding_query_text: MonetaryValue: A quantity of money or an estimated worth expressed in currency. Also called currency amount, financial value, cost, price. Examples: millions of dollars, several million euros, four million (over $4.5 million), $102 million.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryAmount
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'MonetaryValue' and its mentions directly correspond to 'MonetaryAmount', which represents a specific monetary value or range.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

candidates.label: MonetaryGrant
candidates.comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

types.embedding_query_text: Museum: An institution that houses and preserves a collection of artifacts and exhibits for public display. Also called gallery, exhibition hall, archive, institution. Examples: Lalique Museum, Louvre Museum, Natural History Museum, Adrien Dubouche National Museum.

chosen_type.label: Museum
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Museum' is a direct and perfect match for schema.org's 'Museum' class, which describes institutions for exhibiting artifacts.

candidates.label: Museum
candidates.comment: A Museum is a civic structure dedicated to preserving and exhibiting artifacts, art, or scientific specimens. Also called gallery, exhibition hall, cultural institution. Examples: The Louvre, Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, local art gallery. Distinct from Library, which primarily lends books and media.

candidates.label: ExhibitionEvent
candidates.comment: An ExhibitionEvent is an Event type focused on displaying items, such as at a museum, library, or tradeshow. Also called exhibit, show, display event. Examples: An art exhibition at a gallery, a historical display at a museum, a trade show for new technologies, a book fair.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

candidates.label: Aquarium
candidates.comment: An Aquarium is a CivicStructure, typically a public facility, where aquatic animals and plants are kept and displayed. Also called public aquarium, marine life center, oceanarium. Examples: Monterey Bay Aquarium, Georgia Aquarium, a local fish exhibit.

candidates.label: ArtGallery
candidates.comment: An ArtGallery is an EntertainmentBusiness that displays and often sells works of art. Also called gallery, art exhibition space, fine art dealer. Examples: The Louvre, a local contemporary art gallery, a commercial art dealership, a pop-up exhibition space.

types.embedding_query_text: LuxuryGlassmaker: A company or individual specializing in the creation of high-end, artistic glass products. Also called fine glass manufacturer, art glass producer, premium glass artisan. Examples: Lalique, French luxury glassmaker Lalique, the company.

chosen_type.label: LuxuryGlassmaker
chosen_type.definition: A company or individual specializing in the creation of high-end, artistic glass products.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class adequately describes a 'LuxuryGlassmaker'. It is a specific type of organization.

candidates.label: Winery
candidates.comment: A local business that produces wine, often including facilities for grape cultivation, wine production, and tasting. Also called vineyard, wine producer, wine estate. Examples: Robert Mondavi Winery, a local family-owned vineyard, a wine tasting room.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

candidates.label: Optician
candidates.comment: An Optician is a local business that sells reading glasses and similar devices for improving vision. Also called optical store, eyewear shop, optometrist's office (if selling glasses). Examples: LensCrafters, a local independent optician, an online glasses retailer. Distinct from Ophthalmologist, who is a medical doctor specializing in eye care.

candidates.label: MerchantReturnPolicy
candidates.comment: An intangible providing information about product return policies associated with an organization, product, or offer. Also called return policy, refund policy, merchandise return terms. Examples: "30-day return policy", "final sale policy", "return policy for electronics".

candidates.label: AmpStory
candidates.comment: An AmpStory is a CreativeWork with a visual storytelling format designed for online viewing, especially on mobile devices. Also called AMP Web Story, visual story, mobile story. Examples: A Google AMP Story about a travel destination, a news publisher's visual story, a brand's product showcase story.

types.embedding_query_text: TimeOfDay: A general period within a 24-hour day, such as morning, afternoon, or night. Also called day part, period of day, daytime, nighttime. Examples: early-morning raid, broad daylight.

chosen_type.label: TimeOfDay
chosen_type.definition: A general period within a 24-hour day, such as morning, afternoon, or night.
chosen_type.justification: Existing schema.org time types are too specific (e.g., 'Time' for hh:mm:ss) or represent days of the week, not general periods within a day. 'Intangible' is a suitable parent for an abstract concept.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

types.embedding_query_text: DayOfWeek: One of the seven named days that make up a week. Also called weekday, weekend day, calendar day. Examples: Sunday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'DayOfWeek' is a direct and perfect match for schema.org's 'DayOfWeek' enumeration.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: Duration: A period of time during which something continues. Also called length of time, span, interval, period. Examples: months, several days, less than eight minutes, recent months.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Duration' and its mentions directly correspond to schema.org's 'Duration' type, representing a period of time.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: InstantaneousEvent
candidates.comment: An InstantaneousEvent is a structured value representing an event with no duration, such as a single point in time. Also called momentary event, point event, discrete occurrence. Examples: a computer log entry, a timestamp, a single click on a webpage. Distinct from Event, which typically has a duration.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and permanent human settlement, typically with a complex system of governance and infrastructure. Also called metropolis, town, urban area, municipality. Examples: Paris, Strasbourg, Limoges.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'City' is a direct and perfect match for schema.org's 'City' class.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

types.embedding_query_text: CriminalGroup: An organized association of individuals engaged in illegal activities. Also called gang, syndicate, mob, perpetrators. Examples: Burglars, A gang of masked thieves, Thieves, suspected thieves.

chosen_type.label: CriminalGroup
chosen_type.definition: An organized association of individuals engaged in illegal activities.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class specifically describes a 'CriminalGroup'. It is a type of organization.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

candidates.label: DanceGroup
candidates.comment: A DanceGroup is a performing organization specializing in dance, often presenting choreographed performances. Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

types.embedding_query_text: Town: A populated area, typically smaller than a city but larger than a village, with its own local government. Also called settlement, community, borough, hamlet. Examples: Wingen-sur-Moder.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's 'City' definition explicitly includes 'town' as an alias, making it a suitable match for the OIE type 'Town'.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation or state, typically with its own government and territory. Also called nation, state, realm, land. Examples: France, northeastern France, central France.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Country' is a direct and perfect match for schema.org's 'Country' class.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

candidates.label: Embassy
candidates.comment: An Embassy is a GovernmentBuilding representing the diplomatic mission of one country in another. Also called consulate, diplomatic mission, high commission. Examples: The U.S. Embassy in London, the French Embassy in Washington D.C., a country's consulate general.

types.embedding_query_text: Time: A specific point or period in the day, often expressed in hours and minutes. Also called hour, moment, juncture, instant. Examples: 5:30 am, around 5:30 am.

chosen_type.label: Time
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Time' and its mention '5:30 am' directly correspond to schema.org's 'Time' data type for specific points in time.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.embedding_query_text: Source: An individual or entity providing information or a statement. Also called informant, provider, originator, reporter. Examples: investigation source, another investigation source, a source close to the investigation, the source.

chosen_type.label: InformationSource
chosen_type.definition: A place, document, or entity from which information or data can be obtained.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent an individual or entity providing information. 'Thing' is the most general parent for such an entity.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

candidates.label: Report
candidates.comment: A Report is an Article generated by a governmental or non-governmental organization. Also called official report, document, publication. Examples: an annual financial report, a government research report, a UN policy report, a company's sustainability report.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: Quotation
candidates.comment: A Quotation is a CreativeWork representing a passage or statement, often from a written work, attributable to an author. Also called quote, excerpt, citation. Examples: "To be or not to be, that is the question.", a famous saying, a line from a movie, a passage from a book.

candidates.label: AnalysisNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that combines factual reporting with the author's expertise, offering interpretations and conclusions. Also called news analysis, interpretive news, expert commentary. Examples: An article analyzing the economic impact of a new policy, a piece interpreting election results, a report on scientific findings with expert commentary. Distinct from NewsArticle, which primarily focuses on factual reporting without extensive interpretation.

types.embedding_query_text: NewsAgency: An organization that gathers news reports and sells them to subscribing news organizations. Also called press agency, wire service, news service, media outlet. Examples: AFP.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'NewsAgency' is explicitly listed as an alias for schema.org's 'NewsMediaOrganization'.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: TravelAgency
candidates.comment: A local business that assists individuals and groups in planning and booking travel arrangements. Also called travel agent, tour operator, booking agency. Examples: Expedia, a local independent travel agency, a corporate travel management company.

candidates.label: InsuranceAgency
candidates.comment: An InsuranceAgency is a financial service local business that provides insurance-related services. Also called insurance broker, insurance provider, insurance firm. Examples: State Farm, Geico, a local independent insurance agent.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

types.embedding_query_text: Quantity: A specific or approximate number or amount of something. Also called amount, number, volume, measure. Examples: twenty pieces, Around twenty pieces of jewelry.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Quantity' is a direct and perfect match for schema.org's 'Quantity' data type, representing measurable amounts.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

types.embedding_query_text: Material: The matter from which a thing is or can be made. Also called substance, fabric, element, component. Examples: crystal, gold, contemporary crystal.

chosen_type.label: Substance
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Material' and its mentions ('crystal', 'gold') align well with schema.org's 'Substance', which includes materials and elements.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: ChemicalSubstance
candidates.comment: A portion of matter with constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same or different types. Also called chemical compound, chemical, substance, molecule. Examples: Water (H2O), Sodium Chloride (NaCl), Ethanol, Oxygen.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

types.embedding_query_text: Gemstone: A precious or semiprecious stone, especially one cut and polished for use in jewelry. Also called jewel, precious stone, mineral, crystal. Examples: precious gems.

chosen_type.label: Gemstone
chosen_type.definition: A precious or semiprecious stone, especially one cut and polished for use in jewelry.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class specifically describes a 'Gemstone'. It is a type of substance or material.

candidates.label: JewelryStore
candidates.comment: A JewelryStore is a local business that sells jewelry. Also called jeweler, gem shop, watch store. Examples: Tiffany & Co., Pandora, a local independent jeweler.

candidates.label: WarrantyPromise
candidates.comment: A structured value representing the duration and scope of free services provided for a product's defects or malfunctions. Also called product warranty, guarantee, service promise. Examples: a 1-year manufacturer's warranty, a 90-day repair guarantee, a lifetime parts warranty.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

types.embedding_query_text: Website: A set of related web pages typically identified with a common domain name and published on at least one web server. Also called web portal, online platform, internet site, webpage. Examples: museum website, its website, the museum website.

chosen_type.label: WebSite
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Website' is a direct and perfect match for schema.org's 'WebSite' class.

candidates.label: WebSite
candidates.comment: A collection of related web pages and other items, typically served from a single domain. Also called website, internet site, web presence. Examples: schema.org, Wikipedia, The New York Times website.

candidates.label: CollectionPage
candidates.comment: A web page specifically designed to display a collection of items. Also called gallery page, catalog page, archive page. Examples: An e-commerce category page, a photo gallery page, a blog post archive page. Distinct from WebPage, which is a general web document.

candidates.label: WebPage
candidates.comment: A single document or resource accessible via a web browser, typically part of a larger website. Also called web document, HTML page, internet page. Examples: a product page on an e-commerce site, a news article page, a contact us page.

candidates.label: AboutPage
candidates.comment: An AboutPage is a specific type of WebPage dedicated to providing information about an organization, person, or entity. Also called About Us page, company info page, profile page. Examples: The "About Us" section of a company website, a personal biography page, a project overview page.

candidates.label: MediaGallery
candidates.comment: A web page that serves as a collection page for various media, such as images, videos, and other multimedia. Also called multimedia gallery, photo and video collection, digital media showcase. Examples: a website's image gallery, a video portfolio page, a mixed-media art exhibition page.

types.embedding_query_text: Burglary: Illegal entry into a building with intent to commit a crime, especially theft. Also called break-in, housebreaking, robbery, heist. Examples: burglary.

chosen_type.label: Burglary
chosen_type.definition: Illegal entry into a building with intent to commit a crime, especially theft.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class specifically describes 'Burglary' as an entity. It is a type of action or crime.

candidates.label: Locksmith
candidates.comment: A local business specializing in locks and keys. Also called key maker, lock specialist, security technician. Examples: "ABC Locksmiths", "24/7 Emergency Locksmith", "City Lock & Key".

candidates.label: BedAndBreakfast
candidates.comment: A LodgingBusiness offering overnight accommodation and breakfast, typically in a private home. Also called B&B, guesthouse, inn. Examples: "The Cozy Nook B&B", "Seaside Guesthouse", "The Old Mill Inn". Distinct from Hotel, which is a larger commercial establishment.

candidates.label: House
candidates.comment: A House is an accommodation type representing a building or structure intended for human or other creature habitation. Also called dwelling, residence, home. Examples: a single-family home, a townhouse, a cottage. Distinct from Apartment, which is a unit within a larger building, and HotelRoom, which is a temporary lodging unit.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: TakeAction
candidates.comment: The act of gaining ownership of an object from an origin. Also called acquiring, receiving ownership, obtaining, getting. Examples: taking a book from a shelf, taking possession of a purchased item, taking a found object. Distinct from GiveAction, which is the reciprocal act of transferring ownership. Distinct from ReceiveAction, which does not necessarily imply ownership transfer.

types.embedding_query_text: AlarmSystem: A device or system designed to detect and signal an unauthorized entry or other emergency. Also called security alarm, alert system, warning device, detection system. Examples: alarm, An alarm, All the alarms.

chosen_type.label: AlarmSystem
chosen_type.definition: A device or system designed to detect and signal an unauthorized entry or other emergency.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class specifically describes an 'AlarmSystem'. It is a type of product or device.

candidates.label: MedicineSystem
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing different systems of medical practice. Also called healthcare system, medical tradition, healing approach. Examples: "WesternConventional", "Ayurvedic", "TraditionalChineseMedicine", "Homeopathic".

candidates.label: EmergencyService
candidates.comment: An EmergencyService is a LocalBusiness providing immediate assistance in urgent situations. Also called emergency response, crisis service. Examples: A fire station, an emergency room, a police department, an ambulance service.

candidates.label: OperatingSystem
candidates.comment: An OperatingSystem, as a SoftwareApplication, is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources. Also called OS, system software, platform. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is a general application program.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

types.embedding_query_text: SecurityCompany: A business that provides security services, such as guards, alarm monitoring, or security systems. Also called guard service, protection firm, security provider, safety company. Examples: security company, the security company.

chosen_type.label: SecurityCompany
chosen_type.definition: A business that provides security services, such as guards, alarm monitoring, or security systems.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class specifically describes a 'SecurityCompany'. It is a type of local business.

candidates.label: MovingCompany
candidates.comment: A MovingCompany is a local business that provides services for relocating belongings. Also called relocation service, removal company, movers. Examples: U-Haul, Two Men and a Truck, local moving service. Distinct from HomeAndConstructionBusiness, which is a broader category for home-related services.

candidates.label: LodgingBusiness
candidates.comment: A local business that provides temporary accommodation for travelers or guests. Also called accommodation provider, hospitality business, hotelier. Examples: a hotel, a motel, an inn, a bed and breakfast, a resort. Distinct from Hotel, which is a specific type of lodging business.

candidates.label: Locksmith
candidates.comment: A local business specializing in locks and keys. Also called key maker, lock specialist, security technician. Examples: "ABC Locksmiths", "24/7 Emergency Locksmith", "City Lock & Key".

candidates.label: BedAndBreakfast
candidates.comment: A LodgingBusiness offering overnight accommodation and breakfast, typically in a private home. Also called B&B, guesthouse, inn. Examples: "The Cozy Nook B&B", "Seaside Guesthouse", "The Old Mill Inn". Distinct from Hotel, which is a larger commercial establishment.

candidates.label: InsuranceAgency
candidates.comment: An InsuranceAgency is a financial service local business that provides insurance-related services. Also called insurance broker, insurance provider, insurance firm. Examples: State Farm, Geico, a local independent insurance agent.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called individual, human, being, man, woman. Examples: cleaning lady, woman.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Person' is a direct and perfect match for schema.org's 'Person' class.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

types.embedding_query_text: LawEnforcement: The system by which some members of society act in an organized manner to enforce the law. Also called police force, constabulary, gendarmerie, authorities. Examples: police, the gendarmes.

chosen_type.label: LawEnforcementOrganization
chosen_type.definition: An organization responsible for enforcing laws and maintaining public order.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class adequately describes a 'LawEnforcement' body or system. It is a type of organization.

candidates.label: LegalForceStatus
candidates.comment: LegalForceStatus is an enumeration of possible statuses for the legal force or validity of a legislation. Also called legal validity status, legislative effect, law status. Examples: 'InForce', 'Repealed', 'Expired', 'Pending'.

candidates.label: LegalService
candidates.comment: A LegalService is a local business that provides legally-oriented services, advice, and representation. Also called law firm, legal practice, attorney service. Examples: a corporate law firm, a family law attorney, a public defender's office.

candidates.label: Legislation
candidates.comment: Legislation is a creative work representing a legal document such as an act, decree, or bill, or a component thereof. Also called law, statute, legal act, regulation. Examples: the Civil Rights Act, a local ordinance, a proposed bill in parliament. Distinct from LegislationObject, which is a specific file containing the legislation.

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

candidates.label: Attorney
candidates.comment: An Attorney is a LegalService professional who practices law, providing legal advice and representation. Also called lawyer, legal counsel, barrister, solicitor. Examples: a criminal defense attorney, a corporate lawyer, a family law solicitor, a public defender. Distinct from LegalService, which is the broader category of services provided by legal professionals.

types.embedding_query_text: SurveillanceFootage: Recorded video or images captured by surveillance cameras. Also called CCTV recording, security video, monitor footage, camera feed. Examples: CCTV footage.

chosen_type.label: SurveillanceFootage
chosen_type.definition: Recorded video or images captured by surveillance cameras.
chosen_type.justification: While 'VideoObjectSnapshot' is related, it refers to a specific file version. 'SurveillanceFootage' is the content itself, making 'VideoObject' a more appropriate parent.

candidates.label: FilmAction
candidates.comment: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.

candidates.label: WatchAction
candidates.comment: The act of consuming dynamic or moving visual content. Also called view, observe, see. Examples: watching a movie, watching a live sports broadcast, watching a video tutorial.

candidates.label: TrackAction
candidates.comment: The act of monitoring an inanimate object for updates or changes in its location or status. Also called monitoring, tracking, observing. Examples: tracking a package delivery, monitoring a flight's progress, tracking a lost phone.

candidates.label: SeekToAction
candidates.comment: The action of navigating to a specific timestamp within a video object, typically using a URL parameter. Also called jump to time, fast forward to, skip to, go to timestamp. Examples: clicking a link that starts a YouTube video at 2:30, using a video player's seek bar.

candidates.label: VideoObjectSnapshot
candidates.comment: A specific, byte-for-byte identical version of a video file. Also called exact video copy, identical video file, video instance. Examples: a specific version of a movie file, a particular encoding of a video, a digital master copy of a video.

types.embedding_query_text: ArtMovement: A tendency or style in art with a specific common philosophy or goal, followed by a group of artists during a specific period. Also called artistic style, art trend, school of art, artistic current. Examples: Art Nouveau, Art Deco.

chosen_type.label: ArtMovement
chosen_type.definition: A tendency or style in art with a specific common philosophy or goal, followed by a group of artists during a specific period.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class specifically describes an 'ArtMovement'. It is an abstract concept related to creative works.

candidates.label: VisualArtwork
candidates.comment: A creative work that is primarily visual in nature, such as a painting, sculpture, or photograph. Also called art piece, visual art, artwork. Examples: Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa, a Rodin sculpture, an Ansel Adams photograph.

candidates.label: VisualArtsEvent
candidates.comment: An event related to visual arts, such as an exhibition, gallery opening, or art fair. Also called art exhibition, gallery event, visual art show. Examples: a painting exhibition, a sculpture display, a photography festival.

candidates.label: SequentialArt
candidates.comment: An art form that uses images arranged in a specific order to tell a graphic story or convey information. Also called comics, graphic novels, manga, bande dessinée. Examples: a Marvel comic book, a Japanese manga series, a European graphic novel, a webcomic.

candidates.label: MusicVenue
candidates.comment: A MusicVenue is a civic structure or place specifically designed for musical performances. Also called concert hall, live music venue, performance space. Examples: Carnegie Hall, a local bar with live bands, an outdoor amphitheater. Distinct from MovieTheater, which is for film screenings.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.embedding_query_text: Artist: A person who creates art, such as paintings, sculptures, or jewelry. Also called creator, designer, craftsman, maker. Examples: Rene Lalique, Art Nouveau and Art Deco jeweler and glassmaker Rene Lalique.

chosen_type.label: Artist
chosen_type.definition: A person who creates art, such as paintings, sculptures, or jewelry.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class specifically describes an 'Artist' as a role. It is a type of person.

candidates.label: VisualArtwork
candidates.comment: A creative work that is primarily visual in nature, such as a painting, sculpture, or photograph. Also called art piece, visual art, artwork. Examples: Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa, a Rodin sculpture, an Ansel Adams photograph.

candidates.label: Sculpture
candidates.comment: A three-dimensional work of art created by shaping or combining materials. Also called statue, carving, monument, artwork. Examples: Michelangelo's David, Rodin's The Thinker, a modern abstract metal sculpture, a clay bust.

candidates.label: SequentialArt
candidates.comment: An art form that uses images arranged in a specific order to tell a graphic story or convey information. Also called comics, graphic novels, manga, bande dessinée. Examples: a Marvel comic book, a Japanese manga series, a European graphic novel, a webcomic.

candidates.label: VisualArtsEvent
candidates.comment: An event related to visual arts, such as an exhibition, gallery opening, or art fair. Also called art exhibition, gallery event, visual art show. Examples: a painting exhibition, a sculpture display, a photography festival.

candidates.label: ArtGallery
candidates.comment: An ArtGallery is an EntertainmentBusiness that displays and often sells works of art. Also called gallery, art exhibition space, fine art dealer. Examples: The Louvre, a local contemporary art gallery, a commercial art dealership, a pop-up exhibition space.

types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months, starting from January 1st. Also called annum, calendar year, fiscal year. Examples: 2011.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: A 'Year' is a period of time, which aligns with schema.org's 'Duration' type.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: Factory: A building or group of buildings where goods are manufactured or assembled chiefly by machine. Also called plant, mill, manufacturing facility, workshop. Examples: factory, the company's factory.

chosen_type.label: Factory
chosen_type.definition: A building or group of buildings where goods are manufactured or assembled chiefly by machine.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class specifically describes a 'Factory'. It is a type of physical place or building.

candidates.label: Store
candidates.comment: A retail business that sells goods to consumers. Also called shop, retail outlet, boutique, market. Examples: a grocery store, a clothing store, an electronics store, a bookstore.

candidates.label: Brewery
candidates.comment: A Brewery is a FoodEstablishment that produces beer. Also called beer factory, microbrewery, brewpub. Examples: Guinness Brewery, Sierra Nevada Brewing Co., local craft brewery.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

candidates.label: GovernmentBuilding
candidates.comment: A GovernmentBuilding is a civic structure that houses government operations or services. Also called public building, state edifice, official premises. Examples: city hall, parliament building, courthouse, post office. Distinct from GovernmentOffice, which is a specific type of organization within a government building.

types.embedding_query_text: ArtworkQuantity: A number or collection of artistic creations. Also called art collection, number of pieces, volume of works, art inventory. Examples: 650 exceptional works, three porcelain works, 18th-century works, over 650 'exceptional works'.

chosen_type.label: Collection
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'ArtworkQuantity' refers to a grouping or number of artistic creations, which is well-represented by schema.org's 'Collection'.

candidates.label: Collection
candidates.comment: A grouping of various items, which can include creative works or products. Also called assortment, compilation, set, aggregate. Examples: A collection of rare books, a stamp collection, a music album, a product catalog.

candidates.label: PublicationIssue
candidates.comment: A PublicationIssue is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or publication volume, often numbered and containing a grouping of works. Also called journal issue, magazine issue, periodical issue. Examples: "Nature" Vol. 500, Issue 1; "The New Yorker" October 26, 2023 issue; a specific issue of a scientific journal. Distinct from PublicationVolume, which is a larger grouping of issues.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeries
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeries is an ordered collection of related published materials, such as books, periodicals, TV shows, or video games. Also called series, collection, franchise, saga. Examples: "Harry Potter" book series, "Star Wars" movie series, "The Simpsons" TV series, "The Legend of Zelda" video game series. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeason, which is a single installment within a series.

candidates.label: PublicationVolume
candidates.comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.

candidates.label: TypeAndQuantityNode
candidates.comment: A structured value indicating the quantity, unit of measurement, and business function of goods within a bundle offer. Also called quantity specification, offer item details, bundle component. Examples: "3 kg of apples for sale", "2 units of product X as a bonus", "1 liter of milk in a grocery bundle".

types.embedding_query_text: Population: The total number of inhabitants in a particular area, such as a town or country. Also called residents, inhabitants, demographics, citizenry. Examples: 1,500 inhabitants.

chosen_type.label: StatisticalPopulation
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Population' refers to a number of inhabitants, which is a direct match for schema.org's 'StatisticalPopulation'.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

types.embedding_query_text: Distance: The extent of space between two points or objects. Also called length, span, reach, separation. Examples: 37 miles, about 37 miles northwest of Strasbourg.

chosen_type.label: Distance
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Distance' and its mention '37 miles' directly correspond to schema.org's 'Distance' type.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: VirtualLocation
candidates.comment: An online or non-physical location where events can be attended, such as a webinar or online meeting. Also called online venue, remote location, digital space. Examples: a Zoom meeting room, a webinar platform, a virtual conference hall.

types.embedding_query_text: Newspaper: A printed publication (usually issued daily or weekly) consisting of folded unstapled sheets and containing news, articles, advertisements, and correspondence. Also called journal, gazette, paper, press. Examples: Les Dernieres nouvelles d'Alsace (DNA), local newspaper Les Dernieres nouvelles d'Alsace (DNA), DNA.

chosen_type.label: Newspaper
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Newspaper' is a direct and perfect match for schema.org's 'Newspaper' class.

candidates.label: Newspaper
candidates.comment: A Newspaper, as a Periodical, is a publication containing information about varied topics, often published daily. Also called daily paper, news publication, gazette. Examples: The Wall Street Journal, The Guardian, a local community newspaper. Distinct from Magazine, which is typically published weekly or monthly with a specific focus.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

candidates.label: OpinionNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An OpinionNewsArticle, as a NewsArticle, primarily expresses opinions rather than journalistic reporting of news and events. Also called opinion piece, editorial, column. Examples: an editorial in a newspaper, a political commentary, a personal essay in the opinion section. Distinct from Report, which presents factual findings.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

types.embedding_query_text: Mayor: The elected head of a city, town, or other municipality. Also called city leader, municipal head, town executive, chief magistrate. Examples: Christian Dorschner, The mayor of Wingen-sur-Moder, the mayor.

chosen_type.label: Mayor
chosen_type.definition: The elected head of a city, town, or other municipality.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class specifically describes a 'Mayor' as a role. It is a type of person.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: TaxiStand
candidates.comment: A civic structure or designated area where taxis wait for passengers. Also called cab stand, taxi rank, hack stand. Examples: a taxi stand at an airport, a designated taxi area outside a hotel, a street corner taxi queue.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

types.embedding_query_text: Failure: An act or instance of not achieving the desired aim or purpose. Also called breakdown, malfunction, lapse, shortcoming. Examples: major failure.

chosen_type.label: Error
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Failure' aligns well with schema.org's 'Error', which represents a problem or malfunction.

candidates.label: LoseAction
candidates.comment: The act of being defeated in a competitive activity or contest. Also called suffer defeat, be beaten, fail to win. candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

candidates.label: RejectAction
candidates.comment: RejectAction is an AllocateAction representing the act of rejecting an object or proposal. Also called decline, refuse, turn down. Examples: rejecting a job offer, declining an invitation, refusing a request, rejecting a proposed plan. Distinct from AcceptAction, which is the antonym.

candidates.label: CancelAction
candidates.comment: The act of asserting that a future event or action will no longer occur. Also called call off, revoke, annul, abort. Examples: Cancelling a flight, cancelling a meeting, cancelling a subscription. Distinct from ConfirmAction, which is asserting an event will happen.

candidates.label: DisagreeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative opinion or difference of opinion regarding an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express disagreement, object to, dispute, dissent. Examples: Disagreeing with a political statement, objecting to a proposed plan, disputing a fact. Distinct from AgreeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or agreement.

types.embedding_query_text: SiteClassification: A categorization or designation given to a location based on its characteristics or importance. Also called site designation, area category, location status, place rating. Examples: sensitive site, a "sensitive" site.

chosen_type.label: SiteClassification

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: ReservationStatusType
candidates.comment: ReservationStatusType is a StatusEnumeration listing enumerated status values for a Reservation. Also called booking status, reservation state. Examples: ReservationConfirmed, ReservationPending, ReservationCancelled, ReservationHold.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: MapCategoryType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of different categories or kinds of maps. Also called map type, map classification, cartography category. Examples: "RoadMap", "SatelliteMap", "TerrainMap", "HybridMap".

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

types.embedding_query_text: SecurityMeasure: An action or precaution taken to prevent crime, protect assets, or ensure safety. Also called safety precaution, protective action, security protocol, safeguard. Examples: special attention, security, security at French museums and galleries.

chosen_type.label: SecurityMeasure
chosen_type.definition: An action or precaution taken to prevent crime, protect assets, or ensure safety.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class adequately describes a 'SecurityMeasure'. It is a type of action or precaution.

candidates.label: ActionAccessSpecification
candidates.comment: An ActionAccessSpecification is an Intangible item detailing the requirements that must be met to perform a specific Action. candidates.label: WarrantyScope
candidates.comment: An enumeration describing the range of services covered by a warranty in case of product defect or malfunction. Also called warranty coverage, guarantee scope, service level. Examples: "Parts and Labor - Bring In", "Labor - On Site", "Parts Only".

candidates.label: MoneyTransfer
candidates.comment: The action of transferring money from one place to another, either electronically or physically. Also called fund transfer, wire transfer, remittance, cash transfer. Examples: sending money via a banking app, wiring funds internationally, handing over cash. Distinct from TransferAction, which is a broader category for moving any object.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: CheckAction
candidates.comment: The act of an agent inspecting, investigating, or examining an object's accuracy, quality, or condition. Also called verify, inspect, examine, audit, review. Examples: Checking a document for errors, checking a car's oil level, checking a patient's vital signs.

types.embedding_query_text: MonthYear: A specific month within a given year. Also called calendar month, period, date. Examples: October last year, November 2024, October.

candidates.label: Date

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. types.embedding_query_text: Audit: An official inspection of an organization's accounts, typically by an independent body. Also called inspection, review, examination, assessment. Examples: security audit.

candidates.label: AccountingService
candidates.comment: An AccountingService is a LocalBusiness that provides accountancy services. Also called accounting firm, bookkeeping service, tax preparation service. Examples: H&R Block, Deloitte Tax Services, a local CPA firm.

candidates.label: AssessAction
candidates.comment: An AssessAction is an Action involving the formation of an opinion, reaction, or sentiment about something. Also called evaluate, appraise, judge, review, rate. Examples: a critic reviewing a movie, a teacher grading an assignment, a user rating a product, a doctor evaluating a patient's condition.

candidates.label: Certification
candidates.comment: An official and authoritative statement attesting to specific characteristics of a subject, issued by an independent body. Also called accreditation, credential, attestation, endorsement. Examples: ISO 9001 certification, Organic food certification, PMP certification, LEED certification.

types.embedding_query_text: Percentage: A rate, number, or amount in each hundred. Also called proportion, fraction, ratio, rate. Examples: 35% of the rooms.

chosen_type.label: Percentage
chosen_type.definition: A rate, number, or amount in each hundred.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class specifically describes a 'Percentage'. It is a type of quantity.

candidates.label: Room
candidates.comment: A distinguishable space within a structure, typically separated by interior walls. Also called chamber, compartment, space, area. Examples: a hotel room, a living room, a bedroom, a conference room.

candidates.label: HotelRoom
candidates.comment: A HotelRoom is a specific accommodation unit within a hotel. Also called guest room, hotel suite, lodging unit. Examples: a standard double room, a king suite, a connecting room. Distinct from Room, which is a general type of accommodation that could be in any building.

candidates.label: MeetingRoom
candidates.comment: A room within an accommodation, such as a hotel, provided for singular events like business conferences and meetings. Also called conference room, conference hall, boardroom, event space. Examples: a hotel's grand ballroom, a corporate meeting room, a small seminar room. Distinct from Room, which is a general category for any room.

candidates.label: HyperTocEntry
candidates.comment: A HyperTocEntry is a creative work representing an individual item or section within a HyperToc, specifying its associated media and time offsets. Also called table of contents item, media chapter, section marker. Examples: 'Introduction (0:00-5:30)', 'Keynote Speech (10:15-30:00)', 'Q&A Session (30:00-45:00)'.

candidates.label: Chapter
candidates.comment: A distinct section or division within a larger creative work, typically a book. Also called book section, segment, part, installment. Examples: Chapter 1 of "Moby Dick", the introduction chapter, the final chapter.

types.embedding_query_text: MuseumWing: A distinct section or part of a museum building. Also called gallery section, exhibition area, museum annex, building segment. Examples: Denon Wing.

chosen_type.label: MuseumWing
chosen_type.definition: A distinct section or part of a museum building.
